name: Pod
description: Smallest deployable unit. One or more containers sharing network namespace (same IP+ports), IPC namespace, optionally PID namespace and volumes. Scheduled to a single node. Identified by namespace/name. Has phase (Pending/Running/Succeeded/Failed/Unknown) + conditions (PodScheduled, Initialized, ContainersReady, Ready). Lifecycle: Pending → Running → terminal.

name: PodSpec
description: The .spec field of a Pod. Holds containers[], initContainers[], volumes[], nodeName, restartPolicy, terminationGracePeriodSeconds, hostNetwork, dnsPolicy, schedulerName, tolerations, affinity, priorityClassName.

name: Container (in Pod)
description: Single container within a pod's containers[] or initContainers[] list. Has image, command, args, env, envFrom, resources, volumeMounts, ports, livenessProbe, readinessProbe, startupProbe, lifecycle, securityContext.

name: Init container
description: Container in pod's initContainers[] list. Run sequentially before app containers start. Each must complete successfully (exit 0). On failure: pod fails or restarts (per restartPolicy). Used for setup tasks, schema migrations, secret pre-population.

name: Sidecar container
description: Native sidecar (1.28+) — initContainer with restartPolicy=Always. Starts before app, stays alive throughout pod lifetime, terminates AFTER app. Replaces the older 'just an extra container in spec.containers' pattern. Used for log shippers, service meshes (Envoy), volume sync.

name: Ephemeral container
description: Special container type for debugging running pods. Added to a running pod via `kubectl debug`; not part of pod spec. Cannot specify ports, probes, resources. Cannot be removed once added. Useful when pod has no shell or for inspecting distroless containers.

name: Pod phase: Pending
description: Accepted by cluster but not all containers running. Common reasons: image pulling, init containers running, scheduling failure (insufficient resources, no matching node). Diagnose via `kubectl describe pod` Events.

name: Pod phase: Running
description: Bound to node, all containers created. At least one is running, starting, or restarting.

name: Pod phase: Succeeded
description: All containers terminated successfully (exit 0) and won't restart. Terminal phase. Common for Jobs.

name: Pod phase: Failed
description: All containers terminated; at least one failed (non-zero exit or system kill). Terminal.

name: Pod phase: Unknown
description: Pod state could not be obtained — typically node communication failure (NotReady, network partition).

name: PodCondition: PodScheduled
description: True once scheduler has assigned node. False with reason 'Unschedulable' = no fit found.

name: PodCondition: Initialized
description: True once all init containers completed successfully.

name: PodCondition: Ready
description: True when ALL containers' readiness probes pass. Service endpoints filter by Ready=True.

name: PodCondition: ContainersReady
description: True when all containers are ready (similar to Ready but doesn't include readiness gates).

name: ContainerState: Waiting
description: Not running. Has 'reason' field: ContainerCreating, ImagePullBackOff, ErrImagePull, CrashLoopBackOff, CreateContainerConfigError. The most-debug-relevant container state.

name: ContainerState: Running
description: Running. startedAt populated.

name: ContainerState: Terminated
description: Exited. exitCode, signal, reason (Completed/Error/OOMKilled/ContainerCannotRun), startedAt, finishedAt populated. Exit 137=OOMKilled+SIGKILL, 143=SIGTERM, 139=SIGSEGV.

name: CrashLoopBackOff
description: Container repeatedly crashing. Kubelet applies exponential backoff between restart attempts (10s → 20s → 40s → cap 5min). Visible as Waiting reason. Diagnose: `kubectl logs --previous` for crashed-container logs.

name: ImagePullBackOff
description: Image pull failed; kubelet backing off. Causes: bad image name/tag, registry auth missing (ImagePullSecrets), private registry unreachable, rate limits. Diagnose via `kubectl describe pod` Events.

name: Deployment
description: Higher-level controller for stateless apps. Manages a ReplicaSet which manages Pods. Supports rolling updates, rollback, scaling. Strategy: RollingUpdate (default) or Recreate. Stored revisions for rollback.

name: ReplicaSet
description: Maintains a stable set of pod replicas. Owned by a Deployment usually (don't create directly). Selector matches pods; controller creates/deletes to match replicas count.

name: StatefulSet
description: Manages stateful pods with stable network identity (pod-N.service-name) + ordered creation/deletion + per-pod PVC. Used for databases, message queues, anything needing identity. Pods have stable PVC binding via volumeClaimTemplates.

name: DaemonSet
description: One pod per node (matching nodeSelector/tolerations). Used for node-level agents: log shippers (fluent-bit), monitoring (node_exporter), CNI components, kube-proxy.

name: Job
description: Run pod(s) to completion. completions= total successful runs needed; parallelism= concurrent pods. backoffLimit= retry count before Job marked Failed. Pod restartPolicy must be OnFailure or Never.

name: CronJob
description: Job on a cron schedule. Spec: schedule (cron expr), startingDeadlineSeconds, concurrencyPolicy (Allow/Forbid/Replace), successfulJobsHistoryLimit, failedJobsHistoryLimit. Creates Jobs at scheduled times.

name: Namespace
description: Cluster-internal scope for naming + isolation. Default namespaces: default, kube-system, kube-public, kube-node-lease. RBAC, ResourceQuota, LimitRange, NetworkPolicy scoped per-namespace.

name: ConfigMap
description: Non-secret key-value pairs. Mountable as env vars (envFrom.configMapRef, env.valueFrom.configMapKeyRef) or files (volume.configMap). Updates: env vars don't refresh (pod restart needed); mounted files DO refresh (kubelet sync, ~minute).

name: Secret
description: Like ConfigMap but base64-encoded by default + RBAC-restricted. Types: Opaque (default), kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson (image pull), kubernetes.io/tls, kubernetes.io/service-account-token. Stored in etcd encrypted-at-rest if EncryptionConfiguration set.

name: Service
description: Stable IP+port for accessing pods (selected by labels). Types: ClusterIP (cluster-internal, default), NodePort (per-node port), LoadBalancer (cloud LB), ExternalName (CNAME). Implements via kube-proxy iptables/IPVS.

name: ServiceAccount
description: Identity for pods. Per-namespace. Auto-mounted as JWT token (TokenRequest API) at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/. Used by RBAC for in-cluster API access.

name: Role / ClusterRole
description: RBAC permission set. Role = namespace-scoped; ClusterRole = cluster-scoped. Rules: apiGroups, resources, verbs, resourceNames. Built-in: cluster-admin, admin, edit, view.

name: RoleBinding / ClusterRoleBinding
description: Bind Role/ClusterRole to subjects (User, Group, ServiceAccount). Without binding, role has no effect. RoleBinding can reference ClusterRole (gives cluster-role permissions in a single namespace).

name: Label
description: Key=value tag on objects. Used by selectors (Service → Pod, ReplicaSet → Pod). Recommended labels: app.kubernetes.io/name, /instance, /version, /component, /part-of, /managed-by.

name: Annotation
description: Key=value metadata. Not used by selectors. For tools to attach extra info: kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration, deployment.kubernetes.io/revision, prometheus.io/scrape.

name: Label selector
description: Query language for matching labels. Equality (key=value, key!=value) and Set-based (key in (v1,v2), key notin (v1)). Used by Service spec.selector, NetworkPolicy podSelector, Deployment spec.selector.matchLabels/matchExpressions.

name: Field selector
description: Query by intrinsic field (vs label). Examples: status.phase=Running, spec.nodeName=worker-1, metadata.namespace!=default. Limited per-resource — kubectl get pods --field-selector.

name: API group
description: REST API grouping. Core (legacy) /api/v1; named groups /apis/<group>/<version> (e.g. apps/v1, batch/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1, rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1).

name: apiVersion field
description: Manifest field naming the API: 'v1' (core), '<group>/<version>'. Migrating versions: alpha (v1alpha1, opt-in, can change), beta (v1beta1, on by default), stable (v1).

name: CRD (CustomResourceDefinition)
description: Extends Kubernetes API with new resource types. After CRD applied, kubectl get/describe/apply/delete work on the new type. Combined with controllers (Operators) to implement custom logic.

name: Controller
description: Reconciliation loop watching resources via API and acting to drive observed state → desired state. Built-in: Deployment, StatefulSet, Job. Custom: Operators. The control-loop pattern is the heart of Kubernetes.

name: Operator pattern
description: CRD + Controller combination implementing app-specific knowledge (e.g. PostgreSQL operator handles failover, backup, version upgrade). The way to encode 'how to operate this app' as code.

name: kube-apiserver
description: Front-door for the cluster. REST API; admission control; auth; etcd persistence. Multiple replicas behind LB. Stateless (state in etcd).

name: etcd
description: Distributed key-value store. The source of truth for cluster state. All API objects stored here. Quorum-based (3 or 5 members). Performance-sensitive (latency = control-plane latency).

name: kube-scheduler
description: Watches unscheduled pods + nodes; computes binding via filtering + scoring. Filters: PodFitsResources, MatchNodeSelector, taints/tolerations, NoVolumeZoneConflict. Scoring: BalancedAllocation, NodeResourcesLeastAllocated.

name: kube-controller-manager
description: Runs built-in controllers: Deployment, ReplicaSet, StatefulSet, Job, CronJob, Endpoints, Namespace, ServiceAccount, Node, GarbageCollector. Single binary running many controller loops.

name: cloud-controller-manager
description: Cloud-provider-specific controller logic: Node (init from cloud metadata), Route, Service (LoadBalancer provisioning), Volume. Replaces in-tree cloud code.

name: kubelet
description: Per-node agent. Watches Pods scheduled to its node. Uses CRI to start/stop containers. Reports status back. Runs probes. Manages volume mounts. Cgroup setup.

name: kube-proxy
description: Per-node networking agent. Implements Service abstraction via iptables/IPVS/eBPF rules. Routes ServiceIP:port to backend pod IPs.

name: CRI (Container Runtime Interface)
description: gRPC API between kubelet and container runtime (containerd, CRI-O). Two services: RuntimeService (containers + sandboxes), ImageService. Unix socket /run/containerd/containerd.sock typical.

name: containerd (in K8s)
description: Default container runtime since Docker dropped from kubelet. CRI plugin in containerd handles RuntimeService + ImageService. crictl is the debugging client.

name: CRI-O
description: Alternative container runtime, OCI-conformant, K8s-focused. Smaller scope than containerd. Default on RHEL/Fedora/OpenShift.

name: PriorityClass
description: Per-pod priority value. Higher priority pods can preempt lower (evict to fit). Built-in: system-cluster-critical, system-node-critical (for control-plane). Custom: define PriorityClass with value (1-10^9).

name: Pod preemption
description: Scheduler evicts lower-priority pods to fit higher-priority ones. Triggered when pod can't schedule + preemption would help. Eviction respects PodDisruptionBudget.

name: Eviction
description: Pod removal scenarios: API-initiated eviction (kubectl drain, voluntary), node-pressure eviction (kubelet kills under resource pressure), preemption (scheduler), taint-based (taint with NoExecute effect).

name: Node-pressure eviction
description: Kubelet evicts pods to reclaim resources when thresholds breached. Signals: memory.available, nodefs.available, nodefs.inodesFree, imagefs.available, pid.available. Soft (grace period) vs hard (immediate).

name: Taint
description: Per-node attribute repelling pods unless they tolerate it. Format: key=value:effect. Effects: NoSchedule (filter), PreferNoSchedule (soft), NoExecute (also evict running pods that don't tolerate).

name: Toleration
description: Per-pod field allowing scheduling onto tainted nodes. Match on key, value, effect, operator (Equal/Exists). tolerationSeconds for NoExecute timed eviction.

name: nodeSelector
description: Per-pod simple node-label match. spec.nodeSelector: {disk: ssd}. Hard requirement. Use affinity for richer expressions.

name: nodeAffinity
description: Richer node selection. requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution (hard), preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution (soft, weighted). matchExpressions: key + operator (In/NotIn/Exists/DoesNotExist/Gt/Lt) + values.

name: podAffinity / podAntiAffinity
description: Schedule based on other pods' labels. podAffinity: 'place me near pods matching X'. podAntiAffinity: 'place me away from pods matching X'. topologyKey: zone/region/host scope.

name: QoS class: Guaranteed
description: Pod's containers ALL have CPU+memory requests=limits. Last evicted under node-pressure. Highest priority for scheduling reservations.

name: QoS class: Burstable
description: At least one container has requests but not all are requests=limits. Default for most pods. Evicted before Guaranteed.

name: QoS class: BestEffort
description: No requests or limits set. Evicted FIRST under node-pressure. Avoid for production.

name: resources.requests
description: Per-container resource reservation. Scheduler uses for fitting. Maps to cgroup soft constraints (cpu.shares ratio in cgroupv1; cpu.weight in v2).

name: resources.limits
description: Per-container hard cap. CPU = throttled at limit (CFS quota). Memory = OOM-killed if exceeded.

name: CPU throttling
description: When container hits cpu limit, kernel throttles. Visible in cpu.stat 'nr_throttled' and 'throttled_usec'. Cause of mysterious latency without OOM. Fix: raise limit, OR remove limit (let burstable workload use idle CPU).

name: OOMKilled
description: Container exceeded memory limit, kernel SIGKILL'd. Exit 137. Visible in container state's reason field. Fix: raise memory limit OR find leak.

name: ResourceQuota
description: Per-namespace caps on aggregate resource usage. Hard limits: cpu.requests, memory.limits, pods, secrets, services.loadbalancers, persistentvolumeclaims, count of resources by type.

name: LimitRange
description: Per-namespace default + min/max for pod/container/PVC resources. Applied at admission. Use to enforce 'every container has limits' policy.

name: PriorityClass (object)
description: Object defining numeric priority + globalDefault flag. Pods reference via spec.priorityClassName. Higher = preempts lower.

name: livenessProbe
description: Health check; failure → kubelet restarts container. Methods: httpGet (HTTP 200-399), tcpSocket (TCP connect succeeds), exec (cmd exits 0), grpc (gRPC health-check). initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, timeoutSeconds, failureThreshold.

name: readinessProbe
description: Failure → pod removed from Service endpoints (no traffic) but NOT restarted. Recovers on success. Use for 'temporarily can't serve' (e.g. warming cache, dependent service down).

name: startupProbe
description: Runs before liveness/readiness. Allows slow starters longer initial grace. Once succeeds once, hands off to liveness/readiness.

name: Deployment rollout
description: Rolling update strategy. Spec: maxSurge (extra pods during update, default 25%), maxUnavailable (max down at once, default 25%). New ReplicaSet created; scaled up; old scaled down. revisionHistoryLimit (default 10) keeps old RS for rollback.

name: Deployment rollback
description: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/X`. Switches back to previous ReplicaSet. Annotations record revision history.

name: Recreate strategy
description: Alternative to RollingUpdate — kill all old pods first, THEN start new. Used when app can't run multiple versions simultaneously (e.g. DB schema migrations). Causes downtime.

name: StatefulSet ordinal
description: Pods named <statefulset>-0, -1, -2 in order. Created/scaled-up in order; deleted in reverse. Stable identity = stable DNS, stable PVC.

name: Headless service
description: Service with clusterIP: None. DNS returns each pod's IP directly (vs single VIP). Required for StatefulSet stable DNS (pod-N.service-name.ns).

name: PersistentVolume (PV)
description: Cluster-wide storage resource. Provisioned by admin (static) or by StorageClass (dynamic). Independent of pod lifetime.

name: PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC)
description: Pod's request for storage (size, accessMode, storageClass). Bound to a PV. Pod mounts via spec.volumes.persistentVolumeClaim.claimName.

name: StorageClass
description: Provisioner + parameters for dynamic PV creation. e.g. AWS EBS gp3, Azure Disk, GCE PD, NFS, Ceph. reclaimPolicy: Delete (PV gone with PVC) or Retain.

name: PV accessMode
description: ReadWriteOnce (RWO — single node), ReadOnlyMany (ROX), ReadWriteMany (RWX), ReadWriteOncePod (RWOP — single pod). Many cloud disks are RWO.

name: Volume (in pod)
description: Storage exposed to container at a path. Types: emptyDir (per-pod scratch), hostPath (host-fs), configMap, secret, persistentVolumeClaim, downwardAPI, projected.

name: emptyDir volume
description: Per-pod scratch storage. Created at pod-start, deleted at pod-delete. Backed by node disk OR memory (medium: Memory). Used for temp files, cache, sidecar communication.

name: hostPath volume
description: Mount node-fs path into pod. Security risk — escapes per-pod isolation. Restricted by PodSecurityStandards. Use only for system-level pods (CNI, log shippers).

name: projected volume
description: Combine multiple sources (configMap, secret, serviceAccountToken, downwardAPI) into a single volume mount. The mechanism behind /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/.

name: Downward API
description: Expose pod metadata to container via env vars or volume files. Fields: spec.nodeName, status.podIP, metadata.name/namespace/labels/annotations, resource limits/requests.

name: Controller event loop
description: Watch API for resource changes (informer/cache); on event, queue work; reconcile (drive observed → desired). Built on shared informers + workqueues. The pattern operators implement.

name: API watch (server-side)
description: Long-lived HTTP connection or HTTP/2 stream. Server pushes events as objects change. resourceVersion tracks position. The mechanism behind kubectl get -w and informers.

name: terminationGracePeriodSeconds
description: Seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL. Default 30. Pod has this long to gracefully shut down. preStop lifecycle hook also runs in this window.

name: preStop lifecycle hook
description: Run command/HTTP-GET before SIGTERM. Used to drain connections, deregister from LB, save state. Counts toward grace period.

name: securityContext
description: Per-pod or per-container security settings. runAsUser, runAsGroup, fsGroup, runAsNonRoot, allowPrivilegeEscalation, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities (add/drop), seccompProfile, seLinuxOptions.

name: Pod Security Standards (PSS)
description: Three policy levels: privileged (none), baseline (prevent known escapes), restricted (heavily restricted, hardened). Applied via Pod Security Admission with labels (pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted).

name: kubeconfig
description: Client config file: clusters[], users[], contexts[]. Default ~/.kube/config. KUBECONFIG env var (colon-separated) for multiple. Current context = active cluster+namespace+user combo.

name: kubectl context
description: Named combo of cluster + user + namespace. Switch via `kubectl config use-context X`. List with `kubectl config get-contexts`.

name: Declarative vs imperative
description: Imperative: kubectl create/delete/run/expose (do this once). Declarative: kubectl apply -f (manifest is desired state). Declarative is the recommended pattern; imperative for quick experiments.

name: Manifest (YAML/JSON)
description: Resource definition in YAML or JSON. apiVersion + kind + metadata + spec. Applied via kubectl apply. Version-controlled in Git → GitOps.

name: Kustomize
description: Built into kubectl (kubectl apply -k DIR). Layered resource customization: base + overlays (per env). Patches, replacements, label/annotation propagation, secret/configMap generation.

name: Helm (cross-ref)
description: Package manager (charts). Templating + values + release management. Outside this corpus's primary scope but ubiquitous. helm.sh.

name: GitOps
description: Pattern: Git is source of truth; controller (ArgoCD, FluxCD) reconciles cluster to match repo. Pull-based deployment, audit trail, rollback via git revert.

name: API deprecation policy
description: alpha → beta → stable lifecycle. Deprecated APIs removed after 12mo or 3 releases (whichever later). Migration: `kubectl convert` (legacy), or rewrite manifests.

name: Admission controller
description: Plugins running on API server BEFORE persisting object. Mutating (modify) and Validating (allow/reject). Built-in: NamespaceLifecycle, LimitRanger, PodSecurity, ResourceQuota. Custom via webhooks.

name: Finalizer
description: Pre-deletion hook. Object stays in 'Terminating' until finalizers cleared by their owners. Use for cleanup before object disappears (release cloud resource, delete dependent objects).

name: Owner reference
description: metadata.ownerReferences links child to parent. Garbage Collector deletes child when parent gone (per propagationPolicy: Foreground/Background/Orphan).

name: kubectl cordon / drain
description: cordon: mark node Unschedulable (no new pods). drain: cordon + evict existing pods (respect PDB). uncordon: remove. Used for node maintenance.

name: PodDisruptionBudget (PDB)
description: Bounds voluntary disruption: minAvailable / maxUnavailable. Drain respects PDB; can't violate.
